Issued at 300 AM EDT Fri Oct 23 2026

Today-Tonight...A mid-level trough will dig southward across the 
Florida peninsula today as surface high pressure continues to 
strengthen across the eastern US while to the south, a stalled 
front remains draped across the northern Caribbean. The result is 
a continued tightening pressure gradient across the Florida 
peninsula, translating to increasing winds locally through today. 
Northeast winds around 10 mph this morning are forecast to 
increase to 15 to 20 mph, with gusts up to 30 mph possible at 
times, especially along the coast. These persistent northeasterly 
winds may be capable of supporting some isolated onshore-moving 
showers along the coast, though chances remain low (20-30%). The 
best chances remain focused along the Treasure Coast where PWATs 
are greatest (1-1.2"), though it is worth noting that drier air 
aloft may work to suppress development. Towards the interior, rain
chances remain below 10% today. Seasonable temperatures are 
forecast across east central Florida, with highs in the upper 70s 
to low 80s and lows falling into the 60s.

While weather conditions appear favorable overall today, the 
breezy and gusty northeast winds will result in unfavorable beach 
and boating conditions. A high risk of rip currents persists at 
all east central Florida beaches, with rough surf and breaking 
waves of 5 to 7 feet possible. This rough, pounding surf is 
anticipated to result in continued beach erosion. Additionally, 
the return of high astronomical tides begins at the southern 
beaches, with a Coastal Flood Advisory in effect for St. Lucie and
Martin county beaches today. Overall, entering the surf is 
strongly discouraged and caution should be exercised if even 
planning on going to the beaches, especially during times of high 
tide (roughly 5-7 AM and PM).

Saturday-Thursday...The high pressure across the eastern US will 
continue to strengthen through this weekend and into early next 
week while an area of low pressure is forecast to develop along 
the stalled boundary draped across the Bahamas. This will lead to 
a continued tightening of the pressure gradient across east 
central Florida and therefore, even breezier and gustier 
conditions are forecast locally. Northeasterly winds increase to 
20 to 25 mph this weekend, with gusts of 30 to 45 mph possible at 
times, especially along the coast. Wind Advisories will likely be 
needed for at least portions of east central Florida through the 
weekend, and there is even the potential for these windy 
conditions to persist into early next week as the low lingers out 
across the western Atlantic. In addition to the windy conditions, 
moisture is forecast to gradually increase through the weekend, 
resulting in higher rain chances across east central Florida. The 
northeast winds will support onshore-moving showers, and there is 
a low chance (20-30%) for storm development with some activity. 
Rain chances will remain highest along the coast (50-80%), with 
lower rain chances (30-50%) across the interior through Monday. 
There is a Marginal Risk (1/4) of excessive rainfall outlooked 
along the coast through Monday, with minor flooding possible due 
to repeated rounds of showers and training bands that could 
develop. By Tuesday, guidance indicates the potential for some 
drier conditions returning to the area and therefore, lower rain 
chances. Temperatures are anticipated to remain seasonable in the 
upper 70s to low 80s during the afternoon hours and int he 60s 
overnight.

High astronomical tides return to the east central Florida coast 
this weekend and into next week, which unfortunately coincides 
with this extended period of strong onshore flow. This will lead 
to prolonged hazardous coastal conditions along the east central 
Florida coast through this weekend and into next week. Rough, 
pounding surf from breaking waves of 7 to 15 feet, moderate to 
major beach erosion, minor to moderate coastal flooding, and a 
high risk of rip currents are forecast over the next several days.
A Coastal Flood Advisory has been issued for Saturday, 
transitioning into a Coastal Flood Watch on Sunday that will 
likely be extended through early next week. High Surf Advisories 
will likely be needed beginning late Saturday, continuing into 
early next week. Overall, conditions will be hazardous and 
dangerous and entering the surf is STRONGLY discouraged. Even 
visiting the beach could become hazardous, especially during 
periods of high tide.
